functions.note: A single-condition 0/1 select, and the corpus inhabitant of raise/retsink.ts's one-set-arm admission (CLOSED 2026-09-11). The premise this row falsified: return-sinking was gated to short-circuit conditions on the stated grounds that a single condition byte-matches as a merge variable, which is false here — agbcc hoists a one-speculatable-SET arm above the compare (gcc/jump.c:471-502) and for the {0,1} pair folds branchlessly, so the diamond the target keeps can only have been written with early returns. What the row now pins is that admission plus its dependency on the ranked /flip-branch lever: a sunk diamond has no join left, so the unranked primary still emits the arms in the wrong sense.

Long enough that agbcc splits it around a mid-function literal pool, which lands between a `cmp` and the conditional branch that reads it. asmlift’s condition flags are block-local, so that branch has no reaching compare in its own block and the whole function declines at lift.
